$comment: Named, time-limited exceptions for DEVELOPMENT-ONLY dependency advisories.
This file is NOT a suppression list for the production audit gate. The
production gate lives in tests/security/dependencies.test.ts, runs
`pnpm audit --json --prod`, fails on any high or critical finding, and does
not read this file. The two mechanisms are deliberately separate.
1. every entry must carry all required fields;
2. every entry must have a future review/expiry date — an expired entry
fails the suite, which forces a decision instead of silent drift;
3. an advisory is only excused if `pnpm audit` reports every one of its
findings as dev-only. A production finding is never excused here;
4. any dev-only advisory that is NOT listed here fails the suite, so a
newly introduced advisory cannot arrive unnoticed.

exceptions.title: When Vitest UI server is listening, arbitrary file can be read and executed
exceptions.justification: Exploitation requires the Vitest UI server to be listening. No script in any workspace manifest passes `--ui` or `--api`, no vitest config sets `api`/`server.host`, and every CI invocation is `vitest run` (single-shot, no HTTP server). Non-exposure is asserted mechanically by tests/security/devServerExposure.test.ts. Closing the advisory requires vitest 3.x, a coordinated major migration of vitest + @vitest/coverage-v8 + vite + @vitejs/plugin-react across all six workspace packages, which is out of S02 scope.
exceptions.scope: devDependency only — vitest is never installed, imported, or executed by any production runtime, container image, or deployed artifact.
exceptions.removalCondition: Remove when vitest (and @vitest/coverage-v8) resolve to >=3.2.6 per docs/dependency-maintenance/vitest-vite-migration.md, due before S03 begins.

exceptions.title: Vite development server path bypass
exceptions.justification: The vulnerable code path is the Vite dev server's file-serving middleware. The repository never starts a Vite dev server: the web app is served by Next.js (`next dev` locally, `next start` for Playwright), and vite exists only as vitest's transform pipeline under `vitest run`. vite cannot be bumped independently because vitest 2.x pins vite ^5.
exceptions.scope: devDependency only — transitive under vitest / @vitest/coverage-v8 / @vitejs/plugin-react; absent from every production dependency tree (`pnpm audit --prod` reports it not at all).
exceptions.removalCondition: Remove when vite resolves to >=6.4.3, which follows the vitest >=3.2.6 migration tracked in docs/dependency-maintenance/vitest-vite-migration.md, due before S03 begins.

exceptions.title: Vite dev server advisory (same dev-server surface as GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff)
exceptions.justification: Same dev-server-only surface and same blocked upgrade path as GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff: no Vite dev server is ever started, and vite is pinned to ^5 by vitest 2.x.
exceptions.removalCondition: Remove when vite resolves to >=6.4.3 per docs/dependency-maintenance/vitest-vite-migration.md, due before S03 begins.

exceptions.title: Vite vulnerable to path traversal in optimized deps `.map` handling
exceptions.justification: Requires a listening Vite dev server serving optimized-deps source maps. Never reachable: no Vite dev server is started in development, CI, or production, and the optimized-deps HTTP route does not exist under `vitest run`.
exceptions.removalCondition: Remove when vite resolves to >=6.4.2 (satisfied by the >=6.4.3 target) per docs/dependency-maintenance/vitest-vite-migration.md, due before S03 begins.

exceptions.title: esbuild enables any website to send any request to the development server and read the response
exceptions.justification: Requires esbuild's own development server (`esbuild --serve`). Nothing in the repository invokes esbuild directly; it is only vite 5's bundling dependency and is pinned by vite 5's range, so it moves with the vite upgrade.
exceptions.scope: devDependency only — transitive under vite, itself transitive under vitest / @vitest/coverage-v8 / @vitejs/plugin-react.
exceptions.removalCondition: Remove when esbuild resolves to >=0.24.3, which follows the vite >=6.4.3 upgrade tracked in docs/dependency-maintenance/vitest-vite-migration.md, due before S03 begins.

exceptions.title: brace-expansion regular expression denial of service
exceptions.justification: PARTIALLY REMEDIATED. The advisory marks every release up to 5.0.7 vulnerable and only 5.0.8 patched, so no in-major patch exists for the 1.x or 2.x lines. A pnpm override pins the 5.x line (reached via minimatch@10) to ^5.0.8. An unscoped `brace-expansion: ^5.0.8` override was attempted and tested: it breaks eslint outright (`TypeError: expand is not a function` in minimatch@3.1.5) because brace-expansion 5.x replaced the callable default export with a named `{ expand }` export, so minimatch@3 and minimatch@9 consumers cannot take it. The two residual chains are eslint 9 (which itself pins minimatch ^3.1.5, so only an eslint 10 major upgrade moves it) and glob@10 -> minimatch@9 under @vitest/coverage-v8. Both are lint/test tooling that only ever expand glob patterns authored inside this repository — a ReDoS needs an attacker-supplied pattern, and there is none.
exceptions.scope: devDependency only — eslint and @vitest/coverage-v8 tooling chains; brace-expansion is absent from every production dependency tree.
exceptions.removalCondition: Remove when both residual chains resolve brace-expansion >=5.0.8: eslint's minimatch@3 chain (needs eslint 10 / @eslint/config-array >=0.23.x and @eslint/eslintrc on minimatch 10) and @vitest/coverage-v8's glob@10 -> minimatch@9 chain (cleared by the vitest >=3.2.6 migration). Verify with `pnpm why brace-expansion`, then delete this entry and the `brace-expansion@5` override in pnpm-workspace.yaml if it is no longer needed.
